industry_patterns.pattern: Consistently high-scoring sector. April 2026 CIS rule changes created acute, dateable compliance pain. Mid-market software gap (£50-500/month) confirmed by BuildersAI's own roadmap gap and Eque2's enterprise pricing. Two distinct sub-opportunities: CIS compliance monitoring (opp-001) and job costing + invoicing (opp-003). Consider combining into one platform in future runs.

NI's unique dual-EORI and Windsor Framework situation creates a geography-specific compliance need with no current software solution. High willingness to pay (£48/declaration alternative cost). Build complexity is the primary constraint — HMRC CDS API approval and Windsor Framework rule maintenance.

CQC 'Always On' SAF created continuous compliance demand. Market has enterprise solutions (Access Group, Radar Healthcare) but nothing affordable for independent homes (10-50 beds). High pain severity and high ACV (£149/month credible). Longer sales cycle (3-6 months) is the main drag. Partnership with Registered Managers is essential for distribution.

PPDS/Natasha's Law compliance has created demand for allergen management tools. 400,000+ target businesses but low ACV (£19-39/month). Freemium model likely required for distribution. FSA guidance updated March 2025 — timing is good. EHO referral channel is underexplored by current competitors.

Right-to-work compliance has unusually strong evidence of market failure: 80% employer non-compliance rate from official Home Office survey (April 2025). Large addressable market (all UK employers with non-UK workers). Simple build. Strong self-serve sales motion. Main risk: specialist competitors (Uright, Xydus) already in market — pricing and simplicity must differentiate.

45% UK SME H&S compliance gap statistic is strong evidence. Legal obligation applies to all businesses with employees. Enterprise market has solutions; SME market (5-50 employees) is underserved at sub-£80/month. AI risk assessment drafting is the genuine differentiator over generic document packs.

saturation_warnings.category: Generic job management software for trades
saturation_warnings.warning: Market is fully saturated: Workever, Fergus, BigChange, Tradespanel all serve UK plumbers/electricians with job management. Do NOT build a generic trades job management tool. CIS-specific compliance is the differentiator — target builders specifically.
Extremely crowded: Xero, Sage, HiBob, SD Worx, BambooHR, Deputy. No differentiation opportunity without deep vertical specialisation.
Xero, FreeAgent, and QuickBooks are all investing heavily in MTD ITSA compliance. Only viable as a narrow vertical niche (specific industry + MTD) — not as a generic bookkeeping product.
Asana, Monday, Notion, ClickUp, Linear already dominate. Avoid.
LetCompliance is emerging as a focused competitor in the letting agent compliance space. Move quickly or reconsider opp-012. Monitor LetCompliance's pricing and feature set in next run.

recurring_problem_types.description: A new UK regulation creates a concrete compliance obligation for SMEs, but the only software solutions are enterprise-priced (£300-1000+/month). This is the highest-scoring pattern in this database. Examples: April 2026 CIS changes (opp-001), CQC SAF (opp-005), MTD ITSA (opp-010).
recurring_problem_types.signal: Look for recently enacted UK regulations + absence of sub-£100/month software solutions

recurring_problem_types.description: NI's dual position (GB trade rules + EU single market access via Windsor Framework) creates compliance problems unique to NI businesses. No England-based software company has built for this specificity. Local market knowledge is a genuine competitive moat.
recurring_problem_types.signal: Search for 'Northern Ireland' + 'Windsor Framework' + any compliance domain

recurring_problem_types.description: Businesses tracking compliance in spreadsheets or memory face disproportionate legal risk relative to the cost of a software solution. When the penalty for failure is £20,000-£60,000 (RTW fines, CIS penalties), a £50/month tool is an obvious buy. Focus on communicating the asymmetric risk.
recurring_problem_types.signal: HMRC fine amounts, HSE improvement notices, Home Office civil penalties

recurring_problem_types.description: AI document extraction (via Claude API) makes several previously tedious manual processes automatable: customs invoice parsing, allergen declaration extraction, RTW document recognition, care home evidence classification. Products in these categories have higher buildability scores because the AI does the hard work.
recurring_problem_types.signal: Any workflow involving extraction from unstructured documents (invoices, certificates, declarations)

recurring_problem_types.description: Businesses using 2-4 disconnected tools (WhatsApp + spreadsheet + Xero) spend hours reconciling. The opportunity is a single tool that covers the whole workflow. Examples: construction job costing (opp-003), care home evidence management (opp-005).
recurring_problem_types.signal: Search for job postings or Reddit complaints mentioning multiple tool names in same workflow

ai_capability_unlocks.capability: Document extraction from unstructured PDFs and images (Claude API vision)
ai_capability_unlocks.cost_estimate: £0.002-0.05 per document at current Claude API pricing
ai_capability_unlocks.notes: Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 with vision is production-quality for structured document extraction. Haiku is sufficient for simple document type classification. Use sonnet for commodity code suggestions and allergen extraction where accuracy is safety-critical.

ai_capability_unlocks.capability: Risk assessment and compliance content generation
ai_capability_unlocks.notes: AI-generated risk assessments and compliance content are genuinely useful as first drafts, but must always be reviewed by a human before legal use. Position as 'AI draft + human approval' not 'AI generates final document'.

ai_capability_unlocks.maturity: suitable for FAQ/guidance, NOT for definitive legal determinations
ai_capability_unlocks.notes: AI can answer 'is this RIDDOR reportable?' in a helpful way but the legal determination must be a rules-based decision tree, not AI. Use AI for explaining the rules, not applying them.

scoring_adjustments.rationale: Opportunities specific to Northern Ireland benefit from local market knowledge as a moat. Score NI-specific opportunities +0.1 to +0.2 on Ease of Reaching Buyers when founder is NI-based or NI-connected.

scoring_adjustments.adjustment: High maintenance penalty for regulatory products
scoring_adjustments.rationale: Products dependent on HMRC/CQC/HSE API or rule changes require ongoing maintenance investment that constrains growth. When maintenance_complexity is scored 2 (high maintenance), ensure this is weighted appropriately — a 3.9 overall product with high maintenance may be less attractive than a 3.7 product with low maintenance for a small team.

opp-008 (SFI26 farm app, £99/year ACV) and opp-004 (allergen manager, £348/year ACV) have scores above 3.3 but require high customer volume to reach meaningful revenue. For a bootstrapped 2-6 engineer team, track 'months to £10k MRR' as a secondary metric alongside overall score. Low-ACV products need 100+ customers to reach that threshold.

meta_observations.observation: April 2026 was a regulatory forcing function
meta_observations.detail: Multiple UK regulations took effect simultaneously in April 2026 (CIS reforms, MTD ITSA, NHS dental contract changes, tachograph extension). Products addressing these have built-in urgency and identifiable trigger dates. Future runs should track similar regulatory trigger clusters — they create compressed windows of high demand.

meta_observations.observation: CHIEF decommissioning is still creating market opportunity
meta_observations.detail: CHIEF was only decommissioned December 2024. The customs documentation software market is still adapting to CDS. No AI-native SME customs tool has consolidated market share yet. This window may be 12-24 months before it closes.

meta_observations.observation: 80% RTW non-compliance rate is an exceptional signal
meta_observations.detail: An official government survey quantifying employer compliance failure at 80% is rare and unusually actionable. Most market research finds 20-40% compliance gaps. The 80% figure for RTW suggests the problem is structural (complexity of post-Brexit rules) not just awareness. Products in spaces with official non-compliance data are easier to sell — you can quote the statistic.
